visual: Vertical office; wall clock 2:00; lights switch off row by row
vo: At 2 p.m., a Chinese office can suddenly go quiet.

visual: Colleague reclines chair, unfolds compact bed, puts on eye mask
vo: Lights off. Chairs back. Someone pulls out a folding bed.

visual: Top-down office; everyone resting; big Chinese characters appear
vo: This is 午休 — wǔxiū — the lunch-break nap.

visual: Split: students asleep on desks / office folding bed / early commute train
vo: In many Chinese schools and offices, the break is long enough for a short sleep — usually twenty to thirty minutes.

visual: Mei rubs eyes at computer; colleague hands coffee; clock moves 12:30 to 13:30
vo: It's not laziness. Many people start early, commute far, and work late. A nap is a reset. The office doesn't stop. It just pauses.

visual: School classroom / bed under desk / one colleague with headphones working
vo: In some schools, students sleep at their desks. In some offices, folding beds live under the desk.

visual: Wide office, quiet; phone alarm vibrates; people wake gradually
vo: Not everyone naps. But at the right time, the whole room can be asleep.
